title: Which habits weaken monitoring and escalation?
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Original practical exercise with fictional people; never imported, published or shown to learners.
gaps: No published exercise may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The wording, answers and explanations are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical or educational review.

sources.use: NEWS2 report: aid to clinical judgement, record the oxygen device, escalation by policy
Open RN Advanced Skills 7.4: assess the patient first when the ECG changes

required_sources: The unit's alarm and escalation policy
A critical-care source on alarm management, read in full
setup: A fictional shift on a fictional unit.
prompt: Select the habits that weaken monitoring.

lines.text: Silencing an alarm and moving on without looking at the patient.
lines.why: An alarm is a prompt to assess the patient.

lines.text: Recording the oxygen device or flow along with the saturation.
lines.why: The device and flow are part of interpreting a saturation.

lines.text: Widening alarm limits so they ring less often.
lines.why: Limits are set by order or policy; widening them to stop noise hides change.

lines.text: Telling the responsible clinician about a worsening trend even if no single score is high.
Assuming an odd reading is artefact without checking the patient.
